_notes.kit: Portable LYGO LLM Console config. Every path and every port in this kit is either relative to the kit folder or declared here - nothing is bound to a drive letter, so the whole folder can be copied to another drive and run beside the original.
_notes.how_it_is_read: src/server.py + src/paths.py read the keys below. If config/local.json (gitignored, per machine) exists it is overlaid on top of this file, and an exported LYGO_*_PORT variable beats both. Relative paths are resolved inside the kit folder, %VARS% and ~ are expanded.

ports.note: The launchers (LYGO_LLM_CONSOLE.bat / LYGO_LLM_CONSOLE_STOP.bat / PUBLIC_GATEWAY.bat) read these and export LYGO_*_PORT, which is what src/paths.py actually uses. To run a second copy side by side, change port / llama_port / embed_port / colibri_port here (or in that copy's local.json, or in the environment).
ports.port: Console + agent portal HTTP port. Env override: LYGO_CONSOLE_PORT.
ports.llama_port: Chat engine (llama-server) port. Env override: LYGO_LLAMA_PORT.
ports.embed_port: Embedding engine port. Env override: LYGO_EMBED_PORT.
ports.colibri_port: Colibri / vision engine port. Env override: LYGO_COLIBRI_PORT.

_notes.bind: Console listen address. 127.0.0.1 = this PC only. Any other value is refused by src/server.py unless it is started with --lan --i-consent, so a public bind is never a silent side effect.
_notes.scan_roots: Folders scanned for models. Relative entries resolve inside the kit folder ('./models' = <kit>/models), %USERPROFILE% and ~ are expanded, absolute paths are used as they are. The env var LYGO_MODELS declares this machine's model vault and is added at scan time (I:\LYGO_MODELS on the studio PC). Keep this list kit-relative so a copied kit finds its own models.

other_keys.signature: Kit signature string. Do not change - tests and the installer read it.
other_keys.ctx_default: Default context size (tokens) used for a model with no explicit value.
other_keys.ctx_max: Hard cap on context size; larger model settings are clamped to this. 32768 is the native window of the shipped 7B (qwen2.5-coder:7b) - the most the model can hold WITHOUT rope scaling, so no YaRN, no drift. With kv_type q8_0 that is 896 MiB of KV cache (448 MiB at 16384, measured 2026-09-18), which fits the 8 GB card beside the 4.36 GiB of weights. If a boot ever reports ram_refused, this is the number to lower.
other_keys.ngl: 'auto' or an integer: GPU layers offloaded for llama-server.
other_keys.threads: 'auto' or an integer: CPU threads for llama-server.
other_keys.max_tokens: Maximum reply tokens - how long one answer may run before the engine stops. This is the number the portal sends, the chat handler clamps to, and the window budget RESERVES room for; all three read this one key. Size it against generation speed: the shipped 7B runs ~10 tok/s on this PC, so 4096 is ~7 minutes of generation, which is why the engine is streamed token-by-token into the page rather than buffered. Lower it on a slower host, or to keep replies snappy.
other_keys.prefer_by_ram: true: pick a model that fits the machine's RAM when several match.
other_keys.gpu: 'auto', or a backend name to force (e.g. cuda, vulkan, cpu).
other_keys.flash_attn: llama-server flash-attention setting: 'off', 'on' or 'auto'. Measured on THIS build (0.4.1-dev, build 10988) with -ngl 79 -t 6, -ctk/-ctv q8_0, same 680-token prompt: 'on' is FASTER on both halves - prompt eval 154.1 vs 141.7 t/s (+8.8%), generation 15.15 vs 13.00 t/s (+16.5%), and the model loads in 6.5s vs 10.2s. An earlier note here said 'on' was ~2% slower for prompt eval and shipped it off; that measurement does not hold on the current binary, and if a future engine ever rejects it the launch ladder already drops the tuned flags and retries.
other_keys.kv_type: KV cache type: absent means the engine's own f16, or q8_0 / q4_0. Quantised KV is how a small card gets a long context: q8_0 halves the cache for ~3% end to end.
other_keys.batch: llama-server -b (prompt batch). Absent or 'auto' means the engine default.
other_keys.ubatch: llama-server -ub (micro batch). Absent or 'auto' means the engine default.
other_keys.media_root: Where THIS machine keeps the media generators and their checkpoints - the picture engine (stable-diffusion.cpp) and the voice engine (piper). 1.3.2: this build CARRIES the CPU picture engine inside the package (tools/sd-cpu), so when the path below has no tools/ of its own the kit itself is used as the media root and a fresh all-in-one install draws a picture with no config at all. A machine that really has a media root of its own keeps it - the packaged engine is a fallback for machines that have nothing, never an override. Default: D:/LYGO_MEDIA.
other_keys.sd_exe: Full path to sd-cli.exe (stable-diffusion.cpp). Empty = <media_root>/tools/sd/sd-cli.exe, falling back to <media_root>/tools/sd-cpu/sd-cli.exe when only the CPU build is present - which is the case for the engine shipped inside this kit.
other_keys.sd_model: Full path to the image checkpoint (.safetensors/.gguf). Empty = the first *.safetensors under <media_root>/models/sd - for a packaged install that means <kit>/models/sd, filled once by tools/sd-cpu/get_model.ps1 (or FETCH_IMAGE_MODEL.bat). No checkpoint is redistributed with this build: SDXL Turbo is Stability's non-commercial research licence and SD 1.5 is CreativeML Open RAIL-M, so the fetcher pulls from the author's own repo and names the licence it is pulling.
other_keys.piper_voice: Full path to a piper voice (.onnx; its .onnx.json sits beside it). Empty = the first *.onnx under <media_root>/models/voices. espeak-ng-data must sit beside piper.exe - piper cannot phonemise without it.
other_keys.image_timeout_s: How long one picture may render before the limb gives up and names the timeout. Generous on purpose: a first run also loads a multi-gigabyte checkpoint. Lower it on a faster card, raise it on a slower one.
other_keys.sound_timeout_s: How long one spoken clip may take. A local voice renders faster than real time (measured 0.4 s for 3.1 s of speech), so this is a guard, not a budget.
other_keys.scan_roots: Folders this build scans for weights. 1.3.1: './models' is carried so an INSTALLED copy finds the weights fetch_models.py places beside it (the installers put them in <install>/models); the vault path still wins on the studio PC.

image_models.license: Qwen Research License - not open source and NOT redistributable. The kit ships the wiring only and never these weights: run them locally for testing and personal use, and point anyone else at the vendor URLs in `sources` so they fetch and run their own copy.

vae.note: 2.1's OWN vae - the earlier Qwen-Image and Wan VAEs are not interchangeable

llm.note: apache-2.0 - the only one of the three that is freely redistributable

image_models._notes: Qwen-Image-2.1: a 7B single-stream flow DiT, and it is NOT a single-checkpoint model. It takes three weight files passed separately - the diffusion model, its OWN VAE (the earlier Qwen-Image and Wan VAEs are not interchangeable), and a Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder. Paths here are relative to media_root. No separate engine is declared because none is needed: the shipped tools/sd build loads it, PROVEN by a real render rather than by inspecting the binary. Never judge engine support by grepping the exe for an architecture name - those strings are stored UTF-16 and a byte grep reports a false negative. --offload-to-cpu keeps all 8.9 GB of weights in RAM, because the card has 8 GB. MEASURED on this host: without that flag the engine places the DiT in VRAM (4003 MB) and then dies during weight preparation (qwen_image_2_1.transformer_blocks.2 failed) - so on this card the flag is required, not a tuning preference. LICENCE: the diffusion weights and VAE are Qwen Research License (not Apache-2.0); only the Qwen3-VL text encoder is apache-2.0. Check that before redistributing weights.

brain_note: prefer_ids = coder first on this copy (one brain to reason about, fastest boot); gemma4 is the image/deep-conversation route when you switch to it.
tuning_note: Tuned for the coder 2026-09-22: 8192 ctx (multi-turn talk + tool readouts fit; the 7B q8 KV costs ~0.5 GB), 4096 max tokens so a real answer or a code block is never cut off mid-way.
